transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording: available
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sara Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - NexaHealth), Carlos Mendes (ML Eng), Samir Patel (Head of Infra)

00:00 Ethan Park: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, this is ethan park from redwood, i'm the account lead, sara is our solutions engineer, we'll run through migration parity and a quick demo of the API and console and then next steps for a poc.
00:18 Priya Nair: hi thanks, we only have about 45 min, goal is to understand how straightforward migrating from openai/anthropic is and any perf/cost surprises.
00:26 Carlos Mendes: and i want specifics on API compatibility - headers, streaming, chunking, kv cache behavior - the stuff that breaks our current code paths.
00:34 Sara Liu: totally, we'll focus on that. quick agenda: 1) parity mapping for models and api calls, 2) demo of redwood api + console optimize suggestions, 3) discuss dedicated/vpc options and security, 4) recap + poc plan. sound good?
00:46 Priya Nair: yep.
00:48 Ethan Park: quick qualification: are you primarily using openai gpt-4o and anthropic claude-2 for different product flows? or together?
00:56 Carlos Mendes: we use gpt-4o for chat assistant and claude for summarization/longer context. together.ai models aren't in prod for us yet but we test them.
01:06 Samir Patel: infra note - we have HIPAA constraints on PHI, want VPC/offline and KMS integration for key management. SOC2 is a must.
01:14 Ethan Park: understood. redwood private and dedicated support VPCs and KMS/HSM integrations; we can surface SOC2 artifacts. sara will show the security slide at the end.

01:30 Sara Liu: jumping into parity: on the API surface we aim to be drop-in for common flows. examples: streaming chunked responses use the same chunked SSE-style stream with event tokens, and function/tool calling semantics map closely. authentication is via api key header - slightly different header name but we provide a shim library in our sdks that maps openai-style calls.
01:54 Carlos Mendes: so our current code hits openai v1 chat/completions endpoints - any change to the prompt format?
02:02 Sara Liu: message-format is the same: role/content arrays. for the most part you can swap the base url and parity sdk will adapt. we do have a couple of model-specific parameters - for example our kv-cache hints and continuous-batch hints are different names (cache_hint vs kv_hint) but we'll provide a mapping sheet.
02:20 Ethan Park: i'll share the parity mapping spreadsheet that lists openai/anthropic/together params and redwood equivalents. it will include examples for streaming, function calling, and embeddings.

02:45 Priya Nair: can you show the console where we can see per-route latency and token cost?
02:51 Sara Liu: yes, switching screens - this is the console, route view. you can see token-level cost breakdown and latency histograms by route/model. here's an example of a chat route where we pinned a model variant.
03:10 Sara Liu: note on model variants: we provide optimized variants for cost (quantized) and full-fp for latency/quality. you can set routing policy to prefer low-cost variants and fallback to full-fp on quality regressions.
03:28 Carlos Mendes: interesting. on quantized models, how do you handle quality regressions? we have strict tolerances for summarization tasks.
03:36 Sara Liu: we hook into redwood optimize - you can run evals (we'll import your prompt sets) and we'll show quality delta per quantization profile. you can set alerts to roll back or route traffic when delta exceeds thresholds.

03:55 Ethan Park: let's talk specific model mappings - example high-level suggestions: openai gpt-4o -> redwood-4o / redwood-4x (higher throughput), anthropic claude-2 -> redwood-claude-compat or a tuned variant. together models map similarly; the spreadsheet has exact configs and expected throughput and latency.
04:17 Carlos Mendes: numbers please - what's the latency difference for a 2k token response on comparable hardware?
04:24 Sara Liu: in our benchmarks on dedicated p4d-ish nodes, redwood-4x median token latency was ~8-12ms/token; for quantized low-cost it can be 12-18ms with large cost savings. openai numbers vary by model and region but customers typically see 20-30% cost reduction on average migrating to our quantized variants.
04:46 Samir Patel: those are lab numbers. we need a real run with our prompts and infra.
04:50 Sara Liu: agreed - that's why we recommend a 2-hour PoC perf run with your prompt sets and representative traffic. we'll spin up a dedicated trial pool and run continuous batching and KV caching to match your load.

05:10 Priya Nair: about streaming and partial outputs - our UX depends on stable SSE events. any differences?
05:16 Sara Liu: we emit SSE-compatible events and include event meta like delta tokens and prefix cache hints. slight differences in the ordering of function call signals in rare edge cases; we document those and the sdk shim normalizes them.
05:30 Carlos Mendes: what about rate limits and quotas? we have spikes - need burst capacity or fallback.
05:36 Ethan Park: dedicated offers configurable autoscale and burst policies; hosted has tiered quotas. you can set routing to fallback to a cheaper model or another region during spikes. we can set up synthetic throttles for your canary.

06:05 Priya Nair: security - can you confirm data residency for logs and audit trails and how long chat logs/kv cache persist?
06:14 Ethan Park: by default for hosted we retain logs 30 days; dedicated/private you can configure retention and disable logging of prompts. we support customer-managed keys via KMS and can integrate with your HSM. we'll share SOC2 and data flow diagrams.
06:30 Samir Patel: good, we need that doc for our legal and infra review.

06:40 Sara Liu: quick demo of optimize: here we import a prompt set, run A/B across a full-fp and quantized variant, and you can see per-prompt quality delta and token cost delta. you can link eval alerts to rollout policies.
07:05 Carlos Mendes: can optimize run on our private deployment? we prefer not to upload prompts off-prem.
07:12 Sara Liu: yes - if you run Redwood Private, the eval runner can be deployed inside your VPC so prompt sets never leave your environment. we also support on-prem runners for air-gapped setups.

07:30 Ethan Park: let's map a concrete migration path: 1) parity mapping sheet and SDK shim for immediate dev testing, 2) small integration with a traffic mirror to validate API/streaming, 3) 2-hour perf benchmark on dedicated trial, 4) security review and SOC2 docs, 5) pilot rollout with canary traffic and monitor via Console.
07:50 Priya Nair: timeline - we aim to decide vendor for this migration by end of june. can we fit a PoC in next two weeks?
07:58 Sara Liu: yes we have capacity week of 2026-05-25; we'll need your prompt sets and expected qps.
08:05 Carlos Mendes: we can provide prompt sets and a sample of current concurrency (~120 qps) for chat.
08:12 Samir Patel: infra will also need network and firewall details to allow the trial pool to connect.

08:25 Ethan Park: noted. i'll coordinate the trial details. quick head-fake question from priya earlier - about function calling parity.
08:32 Sara Liu: function calling is supported; semantics are identical for invocation payload and response. small differences: our sdk returns a structured 'tool_response' object with a separate metadata field for provenance; the shim will keep the same openai-like return shape. occasional transcription note: sometimes the field names are different in raw rest responses, but sdks shield you.

08:55 Carlos Mendes: any gotchas with embeddings? we use embeddings for semantic search.
09:01 Sara Liu: embeddings map one-to-one; vector dims may differ for some model families but we provide normalization and migration scripts. you can generate embeddings in redwood and backfill indexes incrementally. cost per embedding is typically lower on our quantized family.
09:18 Priya Nair: could you show an example of a migration snippet in node/python?
09:24 Sara Liu: sure - here's a quick python example using our shim: (shows code) `from redwood_sdk import Client; client = Client(api_key=...)
response = client.chat.create(model='redwood-4x', messages=[...], stream=True)`  - it looks like openai calls, minimal change.
09:44 Carlos Mendes: nice.

10:00 Priya Nair: for the PoC success criteria - what do you recommend we measure?
10:06 Sara Liu: primary: 99th pct latency for a 2k token response <= your current 99th, cost per 1k tokens reduced by >=15% (or agreed threshold), and fidelity on summarization tasks measured by rouge/embedding-similarity on your prompt set. we'll instrument perf traces and provide dashboards.
10:26 Ethan Park: we can also run a quality/regression report via optimize and share the CSV for your reviewers.

10:40 Samir Patel: contract/legal - pricing model for dedicated vs hosted?
10:45 Ethan Park: hosted is usage-based; dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with monthly commit - we'll include both options in the pricing sheet. for HIPAA we typically recommend private with dedicated GPUs and customer KMS.
10:59 Priya Nair: okay sounds reasonable.

11:05 Ethan Park: wrapping up - recap and next steps: ethan share parity mapping spreadsheet and pricing, sara schedule PoC perf window and send checklist, carlos provide prompt sets and throughput numbers, samir provide network constraints. we'll target the perf run week of 2026-05-25. any other asks?
11:27 Priya Nair: please include SOC2 and data flow diagrams in the pack.
11:30 Ethan Park: will do.

11:35 Carlos Mendes: one small question - do you support canary A/B at route level with traffic steering?
11:40 Sara Liu: yes, route-level canaries, per-model weight control, automatic fallback on errors or quality triggers - it's in the console rollouts section. we'll demo that in the PoC.

11:55 Priya Nair: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
12:00 Ethan Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and calendar invite.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and minor ASR errors (proper nouns may be slightly off). Links referenced during call: parity spreadsheet (link to be shared), SOC2 summary (link), PoC checklist (link).
